A0071.title: Cloud Security Posture Management
A0071.definition: Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) is a category of automated tools and practices used to continuously monitor and assess the security configuration of cloud infrastructure, identifying misconfigurations, compliance deviations, and security risks.
A0071.description: The main capabilities of cloud security posture management include: (1) configuration compliance checking — automatically scanning cloud resource configurations and checking compliance against security baselines such as CIS Benchmarks and national security standards to identify insecure configuration items; (2) asset visibility — providing a unified view of all resources in the cloud environment, including compute instances, storage buckets, databases, network configurations, and IAM policies; (3) risk assessment and prioritization — prioritizing discovered security issues based on risk severity and business impact to help security teams focus on critical risks; (4) automated remediation — providing automated remediation for common misconfigurations, such as closing public storage buckets and fixing overly permissive security group rules; (5) multi-cloud support — supporting unified security management across major cloud platforms including AWS, Azure, GCP, and Alibaba Cloud; (6) container and Kubernetes security — extending to container image scanning, Kubernetes cluster configuration auditing, and other cloud-native security scenarios; (7) compliance reporting — automatically generating security reports that meet various compliance standards.
A0071.limitation: Cloud security posture management focuses on configuration and has limited coverage of application and business-logic risks. Attackers can bypass monitoring through unmanaged accounts, ephemeral resources, or cross-cloud blind spots. Differences in cloud APIs, permission models, and configuration semantics create collection and rule-coverage gaps, while short-lived containers and serverless resources may disappear before inventory catches up. High alert volume causes false positives, false negatives, and fatigue; automated remediation without business context may also interrupt legitimate services.
